text.p: Scandinavian Airlines System SAS said on Monday it would cut ticket prices on the Stockholm to Oslo route on of its 14 flights between the two Scandinavian capitals.

SAS said in a statement it would cut its EuroClass (business class) ticket price by 540 crowns to 3,300 crowns. Flexibility would be greater, SAS said, and the pre-purchase requirement would be abolished.
The special price applied to all of the carrier's departures, SAS said, adding that the only demand was that passengers had to fly with SAS in both directions.
For those who booked their tickets four days before the departure there was still the SAS EuroTicket, whose price would be cut by 100 crowns to 2,900 crowns.
Norwegian carrier Braathens SAFE recently started daily flights between Stockholm and Oslo, once a route monopolised by SAS. SAS is part-owned by the governments of Sweden, Denmark and Norway.
